profile.campus: Chicago, Cook County, Illinois (QTS Chicago campus)
profile.reading:
QTS's own site places this facility at 2800 S Ashland Ave in Chicago, Illinois, on a 30-acre campus near the city's downtown corridor. QTS plans the site as a two-building facility at full build-out, and as of this registry's most recent check of the operator's own page the second building was still in pre-leasing rather than fully occupied. The campus is LEED Gold and Energy Star certified and uses a closed-loop water-recirculating cooling system that QTS describes as not consuming water on an ongoing basis for cooling. QTS's marketing material also states that partnerships with local utilities cover the site's own energy use with renewable-sourced power, and it lists amenities such as leasable customer office space, flexible workspace, and on-site electric-vehicle charging. QTS does not publish a power-capacity figure in megawatts or a total square footage for the Chicago campus, and this registry has not located an independent source that fills that gap.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, by Chad Williams, and it grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale and colocation platform. The company went public in 2013 as QTS Realty Trust, a real estate investment trust that traded on the New York Stock Exchange. That public chapter ended when Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust led a take-private acquisition valued at roughly $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, according to Blackstone's own press release. QTS has not been an independent SEC filer since, which limits how much financial and operational detail about individual sites like this one is now disclosed compared with the company's REIT-era filings.

QTS describes itself as a hyperscale-neutral wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model closer to peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne than to a company like Amazon Web Services. Since the Blackstone deal closed in August 2021, QTS has kept expanding rather than pulling back, with publicly documented projects that include a 750 megawatt, 375-acre campus near Phoenix acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022 and two large campuses in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, a pace of growth broadly consistent with QTS activity this registry has also documented in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio.

QTS's current portfolio language on its own site describes more than 30 facilities across North America and Europe, without breaking that figure down market by market. No independently sourced, per-building capacity or square-footage number specific to this Chicago campus has turned up in this research beyond the certification and cooling-design details described above.

reading.body:
QTS Chicago is a planned two-building campus on 30 acres near downtown Chicago that QTS has placed in pre-leasing for its second building as of the operator's most recent disclosure. The site holds LEED Gold and Energy Star certifications and uses closed-loop water-recirculating cooling described as non-consumptive for ongoing operations. QTS does not publish a megawatt or square-footage figure for this campus, so its absolute scale cannot be read from the operator's own specs.

The campus ranks seventh among Illinois facilities with published capacity, though that rank reflects only the six other sites in the state that have disclosed megawatts; forty-four mapped facilities exist in Illinois overall, and most publish no power figure. Illinois's six published sites total 236 MW, meaning this campus either falls below that published tier or remains opaque by choice, a gap the public record does not resolve.

QTS is a wholesale colocation landlord owned by Blackstone since August 2021, operating more than thirty facilities across North America and Europe without disclosing per-building capacity. Whether this Chicago campus matters to AI scaling depends on the power and rack density it will eventually host, facts the operator has not released.
